text:
maya: Heads-up — running into a client stall when consuming SSE streams with lots of small partial JSON chunks. Repro: hit the hosted /v1/stream with a prompt that returns dense token bursts, client CPU stays low but queue grows and eventually we stop processing until reconnect.

sam: Ugh. Is that the Rust client or JS?

maya: Rust (tokio). Also saw similar symptoms in a Node repro. It looks like partial JSON fragments split across multiple SSE events are causing blocking while we wait for a full object.

leo: Do you have logs? Is parsing blocking the reactor or just backlog in a channel?

maya: Logs show mpsc::Receiver backlog climbing and the parsing task stuck on trying to parse a concatenated buffer with an incomplete object. Example log around the hang: `recv backlog=512 parse_fail=incomplete_object drain=false`

ada: For Rust, are you using serde_json::from_slice directly on the aggregate buffer? That will error if incomplete. Need incremental parser or newline-delimited objects.

maya: Yeah currently we append bytes into Vec<u8> and call serde_json::from_slice when we see a `}` but that heuristic fails on nested objects and arrays.

sam: Two separate problems: 1) fragmented JSON framing, 2) backpressure (consumer slower than network). Fixing framing helps avoid wasted parse attempts; fixing backpressure keeps memory bounded.

leo: For framing: use an incremental parser (serde_stacker or json-stream) or switch server to NDJSON. Can we change server?

maya: Can't force NDJSON in hosted for all models. We need a client-side robust reassembly.

sam: For backpressure: bounded queue + backpressure signal. In tokio, use tokio::sync::mpsc::channel with a capacity and let the SSE reader await send() when full so we stop consuming until parser frees space. That prevents unbounded growth.

ada: Example pattern (rough):

```rust
let (tx, mut rx) = tokio::sync::mpsc::channel::<Vec<u8>>(128); // bounded
// reader task
loop {
  let chunk = stream.next_chunk().await?; // SSE chunk bytes
  tx.send(chunk).await?; // await here blocks reader when queue full
}
// parser task
while let Some(mut bytes) = rx.recv().await {
  buffer.extend(bytes);
  while let Some(obj_end) = find_complete_json(&buffer) {
    let obj = parse_object(&buffer[..obj_end])?;
    handle(obj).await;
    buffer.drain(..obj_end);
  }
}
```

leo: find_complete_json is hard but doable: implement a tiny state machine counting braces/quotes/escapes and array nesting, but be careful with streaming strings. Or use an incremental JSON lexer like `raw-json` crates.

maya: Nice. Does anyone worry about blocking the SSE connection for too long? If send() blocks in reader, we might hit http client timeouts or keepalive churn.

sam: Good point — set a soft threshold. If channel is > 90% full, switch to a shed mode: stop parsing new objects, emit a metric and optionally close connection gracefully with a 429-style reason or request fallback model. Also ensure the HTTP client's read timeout is generous for streaming flows.

ada: Alternative: parse on the read task itself but offload heavy processing to worker pool. Keep read loop fast: coalesce bytes, push them to a parsing queue quickly. If parsing is the bottleneck, increase parallelism but bound concurrency with a Semaphore.

leo: For Node we do a Transform stream that accumulates and emits complete objects. It uses a tiny state machine. That seems to work in practice. Maybe add a small parser util in SDKs (js/py/rust) to share logic.

maya: I'll prototype the bounded-channel + incremental parser by EOD and attach a micro-repro. If it looks good, we can add a small `streaming::reassembler` util in rust-sdk.

sam: Great. Can you also add a test that simulates many tiny 8-32 byte chunks with split strings/escapes? Those edge cases catch the state machine bugs.

maya: Will do.

leo: If you open a draft PR, tag me. I'll review parsing state machine and test cases.

maya: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rust-sdk/pull/412 (draft). CI triggered.

build-bot: CI started for pull request #412 — rust, clippy, unit tests.

sam: Quick note — add a metric for "streaming.slow_consumer" and emit labels for channel_size and parser_lag. That helps SRE tune defaults and alert on cloud-hosted floods.

ada: Also document SDK guidance: default channel capacity, recommended timeouts, and mention that hosted streams can produce partial JSON fragments; link to parsing util once merged.

maya: Thanks — will include metrics and docs in the PR.

leo: If you hit weird UTF-8 splits (emoji), ensure buffer concatenation handles split multibyte sequences — don't try to parse until valid UTF-8 or work on bytes-level JSON parser.

maya: Noted. I'll include tests for multibyte splits.

sam: Cool. Ping here when PR is ready for final review. :thumbsup:

maya: Will do. Thanks all.
